problem.title: Total 8-colouring of planar graphs with maximum degree exactly six
problem.informal_statement:
Prove that every finite simple planar graph G with maximum degree Delta(G) = 6 satisfies chi''(G) <= Delta(G) + 2 = 8.

The target is the full degree-six planar case and is not narrowed. The first bounded slice is narrower than the target on purpose: it attempts reducible configurations and, as a waypoint, the same bound for graphs in the class that additionally have no 3-cycle through a degree-6 vertex. That waypoint is a step on the route, never a substitute for the target. Whether the degree-six case is currently open is not verifiable without acquisition and is recorded as the load-bearing untrusted status claim.

target_claim.statement: For every finite simple planar graph G with Delta(G) = 6, the total chromatic number satisfies chi''(G) <= Delta(G) + 2 = 8, where a total k-colouring is a map c from V(G) union E(G) to a set of k colours such that c(u) != c(v) for every edge uv, c(e) != c(f) for every two distinct edges sharing an endpoint, and c(v) != c(e) for every vertex v incident with an edge e.

assumption_claims.statement: A total colouring of G is a proper colouring of the element set V(G) union E(G) under the conflict relation in which two elements conflict exactly when they are two adjacent vertices, two distinct edges sharing an endpoint, or a vertex and an edge incident with it. Adjacency and incidence both conflict; non-incident vertex-edge pairs and disjoint edges do not.

chi''(G) is the least k for which a total k-colouring of G exists. Colours are unlabelled: any permutation of the colour set maps total colourings to total colourings, and the colour set is fixed as {1,...,8} for this target.

Planar means G admits an embedding in the plane; no embedding is part of the input and no embedding is fixed by the statement. If the proof route fixes one embedding, that choice is a proof device and must be recorded with the argument, together with the reason the conclusion does not depend on it.

Delta(G) = 6 means some vertex of G has degree exactly 6 and no vertex has degree greater than 6. The frozen class is Delta exactly 6, not Delta at most 6: planar graphs with Delta(G) <= 5 are outside the class rather than assumed to be covered.

G is finite, simple, loopless, and has no parallel edges. Connectivity is not assumed and disconnected graphs are inside the class. Multigraphs and graphs with loops are outside it, because incidence conflicts would then be ill defined.

For every graph G, chi''(G) >= Delta(G) + 1, because a vertex of maximum degree and its incident edges form a set of Delta(G) + 1 pairwise conflicting elements. On the frozen class this gives chi''(G) >= 7, so the target is a gap-of-one statement.
For a disjoint union G = G1 + G2, chi''(G) = max(chi''(G1), chi''(G2)), since components can be coloured independently from the same colour set.

Condition T6 on a graph G is: there is no triple of vertices v, u, w with deg_G(v) = 6 and with uv, vw, uw all edges of G, equivalently no 3-cycle of G contains a vertex of degree 6. T6 is NOT a hypothesis of the target claim. It defines the waypoint of the bounded first slice: the same bound restricted to graphs of the target class that additionally satisfy T6. The waypoint is a step on the route to the target and is never a substitute for it. Membership in the waypoint class is decidable in polynomial time by enumerating the neighbour pairs of each degree-6 vertex.

The operator-supplied planning notes report that chi'' <= Delta + 2 is settled for planar graphs of every maximum degree except 6, leaving Delta = 6 as the exceptional and currently unproved case. This is the load-bearing untrusted claim of this dossier: it has not been acquired, quoted from a primary source, or reviewed, and nothing in this package asserts that the frozen target is open, novel, or unproved. It must be covered by the ADR-0055 pre-research novelty re-check before work starts.

Whether the waypoint class, planar with Delta exactly 6 and no 3-cycle through a degree-6 vertex, is already settled in the literature is unknown here and cannot be checked offline. If it is already settled, the waypoint loses its value as a route and the slice must be re-planned; the target claim is unaffected either way, because the waypoint was never part of it.

The planning notes report partial results for planar graphs with Delta = 6 under stronger hypotheses of girth and cycle type, such as girth at least 5, absence of 4-cycles, or absence of adjacent triangles. The exact hypotheses, bounds, and attributions are untrusted and unacquired. No such result may be assumed as an input, and any of them reused in a proof becomes an acquisition item and an open obligation until acquired.

Every colouring computation is exact and finite-domain: colours are integers in {1,...,8}, extension checks are exhaustive backtracking over finite domains, and no floating-point value enters any trust path. A SAT result is admitted only as a checked UNSAT proof log replayed by an independent proof checker; a solver's bare verdict is not a certificate. Linear or semidefinite relaxations of the colouring polytope are exploration-only and may never appear in a certificate.

A verified set of reducible configurations does not establish the target, and under the full degree-six target this is the single most load-bearing constraint in the package. The global argument, a discharging computation over a plane embedding using Euler's formula to show that every graph in the class contains one of the configurations, is a separate obligation that the first slice does not discharge and does not possess. Computer-checked reducibility constrains a minimal counterexample and nothing more, and must never be reported as a proof of the target. Proving the waypoint does not discharge it either.

A configuration reducible under one interface convention may be irreducible under another. Precolouring only the boundary edges, precolouring boundary vertices and edges, and allowing the identification or deletion of interface vertices are three different reducibility notions with different answers. The interface convention must be frozen before any search and recorded inside every certificate; a reducibility claim without its convention is not interpretable.

formalization.statement: forall G, (G finite and simple and planar and Delta(G) = 6) implies exists c : V(G) union E(G) -> {1,...,8} such that (forall uv in E(G), c(u) != c(v)) and (forall distinct e,f in E(G) sharing an endpoint, c(e) != c(f)) and (forall v in V(G), forall e in E(G) incident with v, c(v) != c(e))
quantifiers: forall G a finite simple planar graph with Delta(G) = 6
exists c a map from V(G) union E(G) to {1,...,8}

quantifier_mapping: every finite simple planar graph G with Delta(G) = 6
the same class, with no additional hypothesis; the frozen class is the full degree-six planar class
some vertex has degree exactly 6 and no vertex has degree above 6; Delta(G) <= 5 is excluded, not covered
there exists a total colouring c with values in the fixed set {1,...,8}
the condition T6 of the first slice
not a quantifier of the target; it restricts only the waypoint proved en route, namely that for all v with deg_G(v) = 6 and all u,w in V(G), not all three of uv, vw, uw are edges
definition_mapping: proper colouring of V(G) union E(G) where adjacency of vertices, sharing of an endpoint by edges, and vertex-edge incidence all conflict
least size of a colour set admitting a total colouring; the target fixes that set to {1,...,8}
admits an embedding in the plane; embeddability, not a supplied embedding
three pairwise adjacent vertices of the abstract graph; facial or non-facial makes no difference
a subgraph H with a frozen interface such that every total 8-colouring of the interface extends to H, so that H cannot occur in a minimal counterexample
a strictly weaker statement proved en route to the target, recorded as progress and never as the target
assumption_delta: The frozen target adds no hypothesis to the planning dossier's candidate statement: it is the full class of finite simple planar graphs with Delta(G) = 6, with no girth, cycle-type, connectivity, or forbidden-configuration condition attached.
Delta(G) = 6 is read as exact equality rather than as an upper bound, so the Delta <= 5 planar cases are outside the claim.
No embedding, no connectivity, no 2-connectivity, and no minimum-degree hypothesis is assumed.
No published bound, reducible configuration, or discharging rule is assumed as an input; anything reused from the literature becomes an acquisition item and an open obligation until acquired.
The condition T6 is not part of the target. It scopes the first slice's waypoint only, and the delta between waypoint and target is itself recorded as an open obligation.
edge_case_delta: chi''(G) >= 7 holds on the whole class, so the target closes a gap of one colour rather than an unbounded gap.
Every graph in the class has at least 7 vertices, since a degree-6 vertex needs six distinct neighbours.
Disjoint unions stay in scope but a component may have maximum degree below 6, so any component reduction moves the hypothesis from Delta = 6 to Delta <= 6 and must be restated when used.
Triangles are permitted anywhere in the target class, including triangles through vertices of degree 6; those are exactly the graphs the waypoint excludes and the target must still cover.
A vertex of degree 6 together with its six incident edges already occupies 7 of the 8 available colours, so the hardest instances of the target are precisely the ones the waypoint sets aside.

success_criteria: one configuration proved reducible for total 8-colouring under the frozen interface convention, with a replayable extension table covering every canonical interface precolouring, recorded as progress toward the target and never as the target

the waypoint proved in full, namely chi''(G) <= 8 for every graph of the target class that additionally satisfies T6, with every reducibility step carrying a replayable certificate and the discharging step written out and reviewed

or, and this is the realistic outcome for a first slice against a full open case, an explicit unresolved outcome recording the smallest remaining obligation: the exact list of configurations proved reducible, the exact list still undecided, the waypoint-to-target delta, and the discharging obligation for the full class, which stays entirely open
stopping_rules: stop when one configuration is proved reducible with an independently replayed extension certificate
stop when a claimed reducibility is refuted by a checked UNSAT proof log replayed by an independent proof checker
stop when the fresh model spend reaches USD 20
stop when no configuration has changed status for two consecutive review points
never promote an exhausted configuration list into the target statement: a bounded enumeration constrains a minimal counterexample and supplies no discharging argument
never present the waypoint as the target: proving chi'' <= 8 under T6 leaves the target untouched on exactly the graphs that make it hard
